prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/one-var): keep `declare` when splitting declarations
prs.author: iamhuman-cheolheelee
prs.body:
## Root cause

With `"never"`, `report_split` (`crates/oxc_linter/src/rules/eslint/one_var.rs:524-551`) inserts a new declaration prefix before every declarator after the first. The prefix (`:537-538`) is only `export` plus the keyword, so `declare` is dropped and the split-off declarators become runtime declarations. With oxlint 1.85.0, `--fix` gives:

| input | output |
| --- | --- |
| `declare var a: string, b: number;` | `declare var a: string; var b: number;` |
| `export declare let a: string, b: number;` | `export declare let a: string; export let b: number;` |
| `declare const a: string, b: number;` | `declare const a: string; const b: number;` |

The first two still parse, but add a runtime `var b` / `export let b` that the source did not have. The last one no longer parses (`Missing initializer in const declaration`); in a debug build it trips the fixer's syntax check.

## Fix

Add `declare ` to the prefix when `declaration.declare` is set, after `export`, so each split-off declaration keeps the modifiers of the original one. The join path already handles `declare` (`report_join` reports without a fix since #25314); the split path only has to keep the modifier. Declarations inside `declare namespace` / `declare global` don't carry the flag, so they are split as before (TypeScript rejects `declare` in an already ambient context).

Alternative: report without a fix when `declare` is set, like the join path. I kept the fix because re-emitting the modifier is enough to m
…(truncated)

prs.title: refactor(ast)!: remove unused `Decorator::name()`
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
`Decorator::name()` was added for the old decorators transform (#2636), which was removed in #2865. Nothing in oxc has called it since. It is also wrong for common shapes: `@decorator(xx)` returns `None`, and `@decorator.a.b` returns `b`, although its doc says both are named `decorator`.

Remove it instead of keeping a broken public API that the JSStr migration (#26242) would otherwise have to adapt.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.title: feat(linter/react/only-export-components): support `allowCompoundComponents`
prs.author: KurodaKayn
prs.body:
Adds support for `allowCompoundComponents` in `react/only-export-components`.

When enabled, the rule accepts a non-empty object export when every property is a React component. It also checks default exports and exported local bindings. Nested objects, spreads, accessors, mixed constants, and anonymous functions without a static component name remain invalid. The option defaults to `false`.

The behavior follows [eslint-plugin-react-refresh#117](https://github.com/ArnaudBarre/eslint-plugin-react-refresh/pull/117).

Closes #27058

## AI usage disclosure

agent summarized the upstream's actions and conducted a review after i completed the feature

prs.title: fix(formatter): keep comments between callee and its opener on the callee side
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Closes #27171

Above PR, which also moved comments right after `(` / `<` and caused churn for users.

This PR only keeps the fixes that are clearly safe.

- Following the policy, comments between a callee and its opener (`(`, `?.`, `<`) now stay where they are
  - e.g. `foo<T> // c` + `(a)` was printed as `foo<T>(a); // c`
- Comments right after `(` / `<` are unchanged for now
  - They need to be decided together with the existing policy for `{` and the other languages
  - The choice is between always moving them to the next line and keeping them in place
  - The policy and the other languages lean toward the former, but are not fully there yet

prs.title: fix(isolated-declarations): support readonly parameter types
prs.author: Pybsama
prs.body:
Fixes #26944.

Optional parameter properties such as `constructor(readonly value?: readonly string[])` currently produce TS9025 instead of adding `| undefined`. Treat the `readonly` type operator as safe to widen, matching the existing handling of array and tuple types. This also handles readonly defaults followed by required parameters.

The change is limited to `readonly`; `keyof`, `unique`, unresolved references, and the existing union-classification policy are unchanged. Unions containing `any` or `unknown` can still emit a redundant `| undefined`; this patch does not attempt full textual parity with TypeScript. Add a diagnostic regression test and declaration snapshots covering arrays, tuples, generic elements, parentheses, unions/intersections, explicit undefined, and optional/default/rest controls.

Validation:

- The new regression fails with 10 TS9025 diagnostics before the fix and passes after it; all 21 isolated-declarations tests pass.
- The 14 declarations in the new fixture match TypeScript 7.0.2 with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` both enabled and disabled, after normalizing formatting and redundant parentheses.
- Strict crate Clippy and formatting checks pass.
- The pinned transpiler suite remains at 20/21 on both baseline and patch, with the identical pre-existing `declarationBasicSyntax.ts` mismatch. Run with `--filter ''` to avoid updating the unrelated stale snapshot revision.
- Full post-commit `just ready` passes: 4,979 tests passed, 161 ignored, 0 failed;
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(isolated-declarations): allow adding undefined to keyof parameter types
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
A defaulted `keyof` parameter followed by a required parameter still reports TS9025, even though tsc 7 accepts it and emits `| undefined`. #27009 handled `readonly` but kept the other type operators on the error path.

The only other operators are `keyof` and `unique`. `keyof X` never includes `undefined`, and `unique symbol` can't appear in a parameter annotation, so every type operator can safely take `| undefined`.

When the rest of the type can't be resolved without a checker, like `(any | undefined) & keyof S`, this now adds a redundant `| undefined` where it used to preserve the annotation. The type is the same. It's the existing behavior for `any` unions, and tsc 7 isn't consistent there either: it widens `any | string` but not `any | keyof {}`.

## Example

```ts
export function keyOf(value: keyof Source = "value", required: string): void {}
```

Before:

```
x TS9025: Declaration emit for this parameter requires implicitly adding
| undefined to it's type. This is not supported with --isolatedDeclarations.
```

After:

```ts
export declare function keyOf(value: keyof Source | undefined, required: string): void;
```

The existing `default-parameter-type-kinds` and `function-parameters` snapshots lose five TS9025 diagnostics. The `keyof` declarations match tsc 7.0.2 output apart from parenthesization.

Follow-up to #27009 (#26944).
